title: Bridging Research and Industry: SmartAgri UGM Opens INAGRITECH 2025 with Precision and Smart Agriculture Innovations
author: Athala Fawwaz
excerpt: SmartAgri UGM showcased its latest precision and smart agriculture innovations at INAGRITECH 2025 (July 29–31, JIEXPO Kemayoran, Jakarta), covering technologies spanning open field horticulture, paddy cultivation, oil palm management, smart greenhouse, and plant factory systems. The team also took part in the Agri Technology Forum, reinforcing SmartAgri's role as a bridge between university-based research and real-world agricultural industry needs.
body:
**Jakarta**. Smart Agriculture Research Center (SmartAgri), Universitas Gadjah Mada, participated in the international agricultural technology exhibition INAGRITECH 2025, held on July 29–31, 2025 at JIEXPO Kemayoran, Jakarta. This participation served as a strategic platform for SmartAgri to introduce a range of campus research-based innovations supporting the development of precision agriculture in tropical regions.

On the first day of the exhibition, the SmartAgri booth located at A303-01, Hall A3 became one of the main attractions, showcasing cutting-edge technologies in smart farming, spanning open field horticulture, paddy rice field cultivation, oil palm plantation management, smart greenhouse technology, and plant factory systems. These innovations are designed to address the challenges facing the agricultural sector in the digital era, while supporting efficiency and sustainability in agricultural production from smallholder to industrial scale.

![](/brand/uploads/a2.webp)

As part of the exhibition program, the SmartAgri team also had the opportunity to participate in a discussion session titled _"Smart Agriculture Technology and Innovation"_ as part of the Agri Technology Forum. In that session, Ardan Wiratmoko, S.T.P., M.Sc., a junior lecturer at the Faculty of Agricultural Technology UGM and representative of SmartAgri, conveyed the important role of universities in bridging the gap between research and the needs of the agricultural industry.

![](/brand/uploads/a3.webp)

_"We want to show that innovations developed on campus do not stop at the laboratory. Through collaboration and technology transfer, these technologies must be widely accessible and utilized by farmers, small and medium enterprises, as well as the industrial sector,"_ said Ardan.

The exhibition also served as a direct interaction platform between the SmartAgri team and various stakeholders, including students, academics, practitioners, and industry partner representatives. The high enthusiasm from visitors demonstrated that the issues of smart agriculture and digital transformation in the agricultural sector are gaining increasingly widespread attention.

![](/brand/uploads/a4.webp)

Through its participation in INAGRITECH 2025, SmartAgri UGM reaffirmed its commitment as a center of precision agriculture innovation, oriented not only toward technological development, but also toward its real-world application in supporting food security and community empowerment in tropical regions.

SmartAgri expressed appreciation for the strong visitor enthusiasm on the first day and hopes that this event will mark the beginning of broader collaboration in the development of university-based agricultural technology.
